messages:
maya: Quick follow-up from today's architecture sync. Drafting an Attribution Fence + Compensator (AFC) pattern to make late credits auditable and minimize surprise billing churn. Wanted to capture tradeoffs here.
ravi: TL;DR of AFC?
maya: two pieces: 1) Attribution Fence (per-billing-partition watermark + sealed epochs). provisional events land as usual. when watermark passes, the fence seals epoch and emits an "epoch_marker". 2) Compensator: an out-of-band service that computes adjustments for late arrivals after epoch seal and emits corrective billing events with full audit manifests.
ellie: sounds similar to finalizer+patches but emphasizes epochs and explicit compensator events. what advantage?
maya: advantage: explicit sealed epochs give strong invariants for downstream consumers: they can rely on canonical epochs that are immutable. compensator events are separate, explicitly flagged, and carry provenance so downstream can apply as deltas instead of expecting stream mutation.
ravi: how do we define watermark? per-shard wallclock vs event-time?
maya: event-time watermark per fingerprint, advanced by ingest monotonic counters + arrival skew estimate. base policy: watermark = max(last_seen_event_time - skew_margin, min_window_start). skew_margin default 2m, configurable per tenant class.
ellie: storage for provenance? we don't want heavy hot storage.
maya: keep raw provisional blobs in cold S3 (90d). For sealed epochs we materialize a lightweight epoch manifest in the audit-db (epoch_id, fingerprint_list, input_ids, blob_hashes, checksum) TTL 30d. Compensator emits audit_manifests referencing those hashes.
ops-bot: NOTE: replay-quarantine and rate limits apply to compensator replays.
ravi: emitter idempotency: comp events must not double-charge. pattern?
maya: use deterministic commit_key for compensator events: commit_key = "comp|{tenant}|{epoch_id}|{fingerprint}|{compensator_v}". producer uses idempotent writes and WAL marker: write wal:{commit_key} -> flush -> emit canonical compensator topic -> write wal_done. consumers validate wal_done.
ellie: what about small tenants where epoching may delay visible credits?
maya: we propose adaptive epoch length: low-traffic tenants get short epochs (10-30s) to minimize perceived delay. high-traffic tenants get longer epochs (2-5m) to preserve convergence guarantees. window is a function of recent qps + SLA tier.
ravi: cross-region events? fingerprint routed to owning partition by tenant-hash, but provisional may originate elsewhere. forwarders ship to owner; epoching happens at owner. audit manifest records source_region distribution.
ellie: failure modes: compensator bug changes adjustment logic. reprocess plan?
maya: deterministic reprocess: take raw blobs for affected epochs, run compensator logic in batch, emit replacement compensator segment with tombstone manifest. include replay-manifest with checksums. Consumers can detect replaced segments via manifest and apply diffs. Large replays gated behind replay-quarantine and will auto-escalate.
ops-bot: ALERT: reprocess runs > 30m will page oncall.
billing-bot: UX: customers want immediate visibility. how do we show provisional vs final + compensations?
maya: API returns provisional immediately with provisional_id and epoch_hint. When epoch seals, API shows sealed canonical numbers; compensator deltas arrive later and are surfaced as separate adjustments with audit links. Console will show timeline: provisional -> sealed -> compensations. We'll add email policy for material billing adjustments > $threshold.
ravi: metrics & alerts?
maya: dashboards: epochs_pending_per_shard, avg_epoch_seal_time, compensator_rate, compensator_error_rate, delta_percent_by_tenant. Alerts when compensator_rate spikes or delta_percent > 1%.
ellie: rollout plan?
maya: phased: 1) AFC in shadow: emit epoch_markers + compensator audit manifests to an internal audit topic (no consumer switch) - 2w. 2) analytics canary reading compensator manifests - 1w. 3) billing parallel-run 72h diff checks, then cutover with small tenant pilot - 1w. Owners: epoching/shard router (ravi), audit-store (ellie), compensator tooling (maya).
ravi: one more: cost tradeoff for audit-db size. we should cap epoch manifest detail for very chatty fingerprints and instead store a tombstone pointer + sampling.
maya: agreed. we'll keep detailed manifests for top X contributors per epoch and sample the rest (configurable). sampling must be deterministic and logged in epoch manifest.
ellie: ok let's capture this in a short RFC. please include commit_key examples, WAL pattern, epoch manifest schema sample, and compensator backfill playbook.
maya: will do. opening infra tickets tomorrow. ops-bot: TODO created: afc-shadow-run scheduled.
billing-bot: +1 on audit links for customer emails.
ravi: +1
ellie: +1
